title: before_compile event is not working as intended on lazy load

labels.name: loader options
labels.description: ORM options like joinedload(), load_only(), these are complicated and have a lot of issues

body:
Hi,

Imagine we have a `before_compile` listener which modifies the query. In this case we have a listener which adds a tenant filter to the query

```
@event.listens_for(Query, "before_compile", retval=True)
@event.listens_for(Query, "before_compile_update", retval=True)
@event.listens_for(Query, "before_compile_delete", retval=True)
def query_multitenancy(query):
    """ 
    Handle SQL Alchemy multi-tenancy.
    Derived from https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/wiki/FilteredQuery
    """
    for desc in query.column_descriptions:
        current_app.logger.info(desc)
        entity = desc['entity']
        if entity is None:
            continue
        inspected_entity = inspect(entity)
        mapper = getattr(inspected_entity, 'mapper', None)
        if mapper and issubclass(mapper.class_, Tenant) and g.tenant:
            query = query.enable_assertions(
                False
            ).filter_by(
                tenant=g.tenant # Adding the additional tenant filter
            )   
    return query
```

However in case of queries that are loaded lazily, this listener is not called. However the more concerning part it is using the filter from the previous invocation


Relevant Models are

```
class Tenant():
    """
    Tenant mixin - (This is not a model)
    """
    tenant = db.Column(db.String(36), unique=False, nullable=False)

class Datasets(Tenant, db.Model):
    """ 
    Dataset model
    """
    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    <snipped>


class Segments(Tenant, db.Model):
    """ 
    Segments model
    """
    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    dataset_id = db.Column(
        db.Integer,
        db.ForeignKey('datasets.id', deferrable=True),
        nullable=True,
    )   
    dataset = db.relationship('Datasets', backref='segment', lazy=False)
    <snipped>
```

Consider the below scenario in a flask shell

```
In [1]: from app.models import db, Segments                                                                                                                                                                                     

# Setting the tenant in a local context

In [2]: g.tenant = '5bcf73ea-9e1c-4ff4-85de-a12257a8239d'                                                                                                                                                                       

# dataset 2 already exists in the database

In [3]: segment1 = Segments(name='Segment 1', dataset_id=2)                                                                                                                                                                     

In [4]: db.session.add(segment1)                                                                                                                                                                                                

In [5]: db.session.flush()                                                                                                                                                                                                      
2019-10-24 21:44:19,674 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.base.Engine BEGIN (implicit)
2019-10-24 21:44:19,675 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.base.Engine INSERT INTO segments (tenant, dataset_id, name, users, matched, score, theme, filter, is_deleted, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (%(tenant)s, %(dataset_id)s, %(name)s, %(users)s, %(matched)s, %(score)s, %(theme)s, %(filter)s, %(is_deleted)s, now(), now()) RETURNING segments.id
2019-10-24 21:44:19,675 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.base.Engine {'tenant': '5bcf73ea-9e1c-4ff4-85de-a12257a8239d', 'dataset_id': 2, 'name': 'Segment 1', 'users': None, 'matched': None, 'score': None, 'theme': 'light', 'filter': None, 'is_deleted': False}

# Trying to access the Parent entity

In [6]: segment1.dataset                                                                                                                                                                                                        
2019-10-24 21:44:49,238 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.base.Engine SELECT datasets.tenant AS datasets_tenant, datasets.id AS datasets_id, datasets.name AS datasets_name, datasets.status AS datasets_status, datasets.payload AS datasets_payload, datasets.integration_id AS datasets_integration_id, datasets.is_deleted AS datasets_is_deleted, datasets.created_at AS datasets_created_at, datasets.updated_at AS datasets_updated_at, integrations_1.id AS integrations_1_id, integrations_1.name AS integrations_1_name, integrations_1.code AS integrations_1_code 
FROM datasets LEFT OUTER JOIN integrations AS integrations_1 ON integrations_1.id = datasets.integration_id 
WHERE datasets.id = %(param_1)s AND datasets.tenant = %(tenant_1)s
2019-10-24 21:44:49,238 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.base.Engine {'param_1': 2, 'tenant_1': '5bcf73ea-9e1c-4ff4-85de-a12257a8239d'}  # The tenant is correctly bound
Out[6]: <Datasets 2>

# Setting a new tenant

In [7]: g.tenant = '68181ebe-2034-4e2c-87b8-6c6327e158c6'                                                                                                                                                                       

In [8]: segment2 = Segments(name='Segment 2', dataset_id=20)                                                                                                                                                                    

In [9]: db.session.add(segment2)                                                                                                                                                                                                

In [10]: db.session.flush()                                                                                                                                                                                                     
2019-10-24 21:45:34,896 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.base.Engine INSERT INTO segments (tenant, dataset_id, name, users, matched, score, theme, filter, is_deleted, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (%(tenant)s, %(dataset_id)s, %(name)s, %(users)s, %(matched)s, %(score)s, %(theme)s, %(filter)s, %(is_deleted)s, now(), now()) RETURNING segments.id
2019-10-24 21:45:34,897 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.base.Engine {'tenant': '68181ebe-2034-4e2c-87b8-6c6327e158c6', 'dataset_id': 20, 'name': 'Segment 2', 'users': None, 'matched': None, 'score': None, 'theme': 'light', 'filter': None, 'is_deleted': False}

In [11]: segment2.dataset                                                                                                                                                                                                       
2019-10-24 21:45:42,179 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.base.Engine SELECT datasets.tenant AS datasets_tenant, datasets.id AS datasets_id, datasets.name AS datasets_name, datasets.status AS datasets_status, datasets.payload AS datasets_payload, datasets.integration_id AS datasets_integration_id, datasets.is_deleted AS datasets_is_deleted, datasets.created_at AS datasets_created_at, datasets.updated_at AS datasets_updated_at, integrations_1.id AS integrations_1_id, integrations_1.name AS integrations_1_name, integrations_1.code AS integrations_1_code 
FROM datasets LEFT OUTER JOIN integrations AS integrations_1 ON integrations_1.id = datasets.integration_id 
WHERE datasets.id = %(param_1)s AND datasets.tenant = %(tenant_1)s
2019-10-24 21:45:42,179 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.base.Engine {'param_1': 20, 'tenant_1': '5bcf73ea-9e1c-4ff4-85de-a12257a8239d'}   # It still points to the old tenant.
```

As you can see when dataset was lazily loaded in statement 11, it used the previous tenant instead of invoking the `before_compile` listener and using the right tenant

Cheers
